title: Quarterly roadmap review, three hours
covers: a three-hour meeting, written as checkpoint notes and merged
decisions in the first, middle and last hour
a later decision that replaces an earlier one
long stretches of discussion with nothing to note

segments.speaker: Alex Example
segments.text: Welcome to the quarterly roadmap review. It's a long one, we have three hours booked.

segments.speaker: Dev Example
segments.text: First, the public beta. We decided last week to launch the beta on May 4.

segments.speaker: Alex Example
segments.text: Confirmed, the beta launch stays on May 4 for now.

segments.speaker: Sam Example
segments.text: I'll prepare the beta announcement draft by April 20.

segments.speaker: Riley Example
segments.text: Back to pricing. We agreed the team plan stays at the current price this year.

segments.speaker: Jordan Example
segments.text: Yes, no price change for the team plan in this calendar year.

segments.speaker: Jordan Example
segments.text: I'll update the pricing page FAQ by the end of the month.

segments.speaker: Dev Example
segments.text: Bad news on the beta. The security review will not finish before May 4.

segments.speaker: Alex Example
segments.text: Then we move the beta launch to May 18. That replaces the May 4 date.

segments.speaker: Sam Example
segments.text: Then I'll move the announcement draft to May 8.

segments.speaker: Riley Example
segments.text: Last item, data residency. We are not offering an EU region this year.

segments.speaker: Alex Example
segments.text: Right, the EU region is out of scope for this year. We revisit it in January.

segments.speaker: Jordan Example
segments.text: Riley, can you write the customer note about the EU region by Friday?

segments.speaker: Riley Example
segments.text: Yes, I'll write it by Friday.
